population.rule: matched positive-numeric log core with prune-only native tips >=40

interpretation: Even when each system is deliberately estimated from only half its species, measurement-induced trait-order reversal is much lower than full-data cross-family re-ordering. Because half-sample rho estimates are noisier than the full-data estimates used in the biological comparison, this split-half analysis is conservative with respect to the measurement-noise explanation. Estimator instability therefore cannot account for the near-half observed cross-lineage re-ordering.
hard_nonclaims: Measurement-only and biological reversal probabilities are not additive, so observed minus split-half reversal is not interpreted as an exact biological fraction.
Split-half reliability does not identify the ecological mechanism of re-ordering.
This is a post-outcome exploratory reliability analysis.

conservative_sign_flip_correction.assumption: Treat the half-sample within-family order-disagreement rate as if it were the full-data pairwise measurement-disagreement rate. Because each half uses fewer species than the actual full-data estimates, this deliberately overstates full-data measurement instability.
conservative_sign_flip_correction.interpretation: Even under this deliberately pessimistic symmetric independent sign-flip approximation, latent cross-family re-ordering remains very high.
conservative_sign_flip_correction.role: illustrative sensitivity, not a formal measurement-error model
